source.title: Guided by the Plan: Enhancing Faithful Autoregressive Text-to-Audio Generation with Guided Decoding
source.authors: Jun-Cheng Wang; Zhe Hu; Chao Xu; Siyue Ren; Yu-Xiang Feng; Yang Liu; Bai-Gui Sun; Shu-Jun Wang

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study probes early autoregressive audio-token representations for information about global properties of later generated audio. This is a conceptual test of the incidental/local-feature explanation in V6, but it does not use the claim’s rhyme-word intervention or test future-token decoding directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports prefix probes for event count and object category, plus comparisons using real-audio tokens and decoded prefix audio. These are recorded below. Guided-decoding performance results are not recorded as evidence for the claim: prefix selection is deliberately induced by a separately trained critic, and the study does not intervene on the generator’s planning representation itself.
record.test_reason: The study probes penultimate-layer prefix states (first 32 of 288 steps) of an autoregressive text-to-audio generator (Siren). The probes predict global attributes of the full output: event count and object category. This is a probing test of internal look-ahead in a new task and architecture, which bears on V5. It is not token decoding (V2), not rhyme planning (V1/V4), and has no intervention showing the representation steers generation or is computed for later use (V3/V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim AR text-to-audio models 'inherently perform implicit planning', with early tokens encoding global attributes of the full output. They use this to train Plan-Critic for prefix-first guided sampling, reporting up to a 10-point CLAP gain over Siren (36.47 vs 26.67) at equal token budget.
record.recipe_differences: Uses MLP probes on AR audio-token representations to predict global attributes; it does not use rhyme-word interventions or directly intervene on a language-model planning feature.
record.method_sensitivity: The study contrasts generated prefixes with tokens from real-world ground-truth audio and with audio decoded from generated prefixes; predictive results differ across these input conditions. Prefix length is 32 steps in the principal probe.

fits_no_version.finding: For fixed prefixes, mean CLAP over 1,000 completions spans [−10, 20], while the standard deviation clusters in [2, 3].
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In AR audio generation, output instruction-following quality is largely fixed by the early prefix.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The main attribute probes use MLPs and do not establish causal use of the probed information. Event-count labels are produced using a multimodal LLM, and object-category prompts are generated with a language model. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the probe results. The paper’s Figure 5 text gives ranges but does not provide detailed numerical summaries or a clear reference for the mean range.
record.rows_left_out: Guided-decoding CLAP comparisons and ablations (Tables 1–7 and 9) are not included as rows because they evaluate a deliberately imposed critic-based prefix-selection method, rather than the generator’s native causal use of a planning representation.

untested.parts: No verse, rhyme words, or frontier-model attribution.
No decoding of specific future tokens from a single hidden state; probes use 32-step prefix states to predict global attributes.
No test that features are computed for their later use rather than as a side effect.

There is no intervention on the probed representation and no prompt-only control. So the study cannot separate a steering plan from prompt encoding carried in the hidden states, and no horizon analysis is given.

missing.what: No prompt-only or text-embedding-only probe control. Without it, readers cannot tell whether prefix states encode a plan or just the conditioning prompt; this matters for V5 and V6 interpretation.
Critic timing ablation: applying the critic at prefix-32 gives 27.52 CLAP versus about 18 at later steps. This is a critic-method result and only indirect evidence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked everything to V6 and labelled it challenges. That label is not warranted. The study never intervenes on the representation, and its controls (decoded audio via VGGish; real-audio tokens) lack the text prompt. The predictive signal in R1–R4 could therefore reflect prompt conditioning rather than a plan, which is especially likely for object category, whose labels come from the prompt captions. The better fit is V5 as a probing-only result in a new domain. Guided-decoding results are correctly excluded. Appendix Strategy (v), described as no intermediate critique, equals the full method's 36.47 CLAP, an internal inconsistency.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming verse, candidate rhyme-word representation, or intervention on rhyme words.
The probes predict global audio attributes, not tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state.

The study does not establish that the generator computes a feature because it will be useful at later positions, rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction. Critic-guided prefix selection is an imposed inference procedure, not a test of the generator’s native use of such features.
No open-weight text model rhyme-planning test or attribution-graph/probing-tool analysis.
The study concerns text-to-audio generation, not multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or the listed other tasks and architectures.

Tests whether early generated audio-token representations predict global attributes and whether those signals are explained by decoded/local audio content. Does not intervene on the representation to establish that it causally steers the generator’s subsequent tokens, or determine the maximum planning horizon.

relationships.condition: Siren AR text-to-audio generator, penultimate-layer states of the first 32 of 288 steps, held-out split
relationships.reason: Held-out probes predict full-output event count (K 0.72, P 0.85) and object category (81.41%), while the decoded-prefix-audio control fails (R2, R4, R7, R8). Evidence is correlational only and possibly prompt-driven.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out probes using the first 32 of 288 steps predicted full-output event totals with K=0.72 and P=0.85 and object categories with 81.41% accuracy, while decoded prefix audio failed, although the evidence remained correlational and potentially driven by the prompt.

labels.reason: R2 and R4 establish held-out global-attribute decodability from early states; R7 and R8 show failure of decoded-prefix audio features. This supports V5 in the tested setting, with the stated correlational and prompt-conditioning caveats.

relation.reason: Section 2.2 directly probes whether early generator representations predict global attributes of complete outputs; Section 4.3 supplies comparison controls.

tranche.reason: The paper reports its own early-state probing results in a new setting, autoregressive text-to-audio generation.

source_check.notes: Siren is explicitly a parallel causal transformer, so this adds a modality rather than evidence for a non-transformer architecture. R6's small positive correlations support its quantitative partial designation, although the authors describe the control as failing; no prompt-only control or prompt-disjoint probing split is specified.

statements.correction: Figure 2: test event-count K=0.72, S=0.86, P=0.85; test object-category accuracy=81.41%. Figure 4: decoded-prefix test K=0.02. Abstract: repository URL provided; code availability stated prospectively. EACL review status: not stated.
statements.problem: The experimental claims match the text. EACL review status and available code are not established by the supplied paper; it provides a repository URL and describes code availability prospectively.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Siren generated prefixes, first 32 steps; event-count and sound-object attributes
reader_labels.reason: Generated prefixes predict global attributes on held-out data, while decoded-prefix-audio controls have near-zero correlations, challenging a purely local decoded-content explanation (R2, R4, R7, R8). This does not establish causal steering.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Real-world ground-truth audio tokens encoded by Siren
reader_labels.reason: The real-audio-token control has substantially weaker correlations than generated prefixes, but the reported values are nonzero; the result does not support a general claim that such information is absent from local tokens (R5, R6).
